summary: Three well-written passages of about 820 words in true IELTS style, rising from a history text to a psychology argument, with a good mix of question types. Three groups of questions were out of passage order (which real IELTS never does), and I have put them in order. Passage 1 is on the easy side because some questions copy the passage word for word.
strengths: Passage lengths (826, 816, 826 words) and register are right; Passage 3 ('The scent of the past') has C1 vocabulary and a real argument with sceptical counter-evidence.
Good question mix: sentence completion, T/F/NG, matching information, summary completion, matching people with an extra name, MCQ, Y/N/NG, and a summary with a word list.
MCQ distractors are well built: Q29 A and B are explicitly ruled out ('not produced any faster', 'no richer in checkable detail'), and C reverses the passage (people are more confident, not less).
NOT GIVEN items are genuinely unaddressed (road-building time, bridges in use today, Proust being first).

issues.problem: Sentence completion Q5 (milestones) and Q6 (soldiers) were out of passage order: the passage mentions soldiers first.
issues.change: Swapped the two items so Q5 = soldiers, Q6 = milestones; numbering and type kept.

issues.problem: Summary gaps 19 (noise) and 20 (direction) were out of passage order: paragraph C gives 'any direction' before the noise point. The summary also credited the noise to the horizontal-axis machine's 'fast-moving blade tips', which the passage only implies.
issues.change: Rewrote the two summary lines: 19 = 'accepts wind from any ____ without turning' (direction), 20 = 'its slower blade tips also make far less of the aerodynamic ____' (noise). Explanations and evidence moved with them.

issues.problem: Y/N/NG Q31 (anatomy, paragraph 2) came before Q32 (Proust, paragraph 1): out of passage order.
issues.change: Swapped: Q31 = Proust first to notice (NOT GIVEN), Q32 = direct connection physically real (YES).

issues.problem: Pair's question side 'earlier in life' is not in option D ('date from earlier in a person's life').
issues.change: Pair now ['cluster in the first decade of life', 'date from earlier in a person's life'].

issues.problem: Pair's question side 'early childhood' is not visible to the student (the summary reads 'early {{38}}'; childhood is the answer).
issues.change: Pair now ['most densely before the age of ten', 'most often into early'].

issues.problem: Q1, Q2 and Q7 copy the passage almost word for word ('marked out on the ground with wooden', 'relay stations'); the explanation for Q2 even says so. Passage 1 completion is easier than IELTS.
issues.change: Suggest e.g. Q2 'Wooden ______ showed workers where the road would go.'

issues.problem: Summary gap 22 repeats 'a few per cent of a household's annual' exactly.
issues.change: Suggest 'covers only a tiny share of what a home uses in a year: its annual ______'.
